gen-gf-unica-one-inter: Distinctive from the first glance: Unica One keeps every stroke uniform, with a very large lowercase eye and daylight in each curve. Inter's smooth, tube-like lines take over, a sans with generous counters.
gen-irish-grover-roboto-slab: Precise and structured, the slab-serif body lets its middle zone dominate, while Irish Grover goes fun and sturdy. Roboto Slab keeps its open throats clear when you size it down a notch.
gen-irish-grover-rubik: Tall lowercase makes Irish Grover words look sturdy and large, with softly varied strokes. Rubik is the soft, clean one, with round letters that stay clear at small sizes.
gen-luckiest-guy-bitter: Bitter reads dependable and grounded, its very large lowercase eye and see-through s giving text a firm footing. Yet Luckiest Guy's cheerful, wire-weight shout against that sturdy slab-serif is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-gf-metamorphous-mulish: Commanding without hairline fuss, Metamorphous keeps a tempered thick-thin variation and a high midline. Mulish is the modern, approachable one, with no modulation at all and a large x-height.
gen-gf-wallpoet-instrument-sans: Bold, with lowercase that rises high and paper showing between letters, Wallpoet is the loud one. Instrument Sans keeps things clean and modern, its stroke weight never varying from letter to letter.
gen-gf-warnes-inter: Expressive ink strokes: Warnes tapers each one out before touching, with no stroke contrast and stretched, spacious tracking. Warnes earns its keep big and short, while Inter handles the rest.
gen-gf-oxanium-mulish: Mulish is modern and approachable, with apertures that open wide like a horseshoe magnet and no thick-and-thin modulation. Mulish stays out of the way while Oxanium commands attention with uninterrupted monoline strokes.
gen-luckiest-guy-roboto-slab: Roboto Slab reads precise and structured, with a middle zone that dominates the line and open throats in its rounder letters. Luckiest Guy brings the loud, cheerful, tubular shout up top.
gen-megrim-bitter: Megrim is angular and futuristic, every stroke ending at a measured thickness, like cable bent into shapes. Bitter makes extended reading feel grounded, thanks to its large lowercase eye.
